## 2. In-Flight Work

- Issues #12 and #13 (registry) are fixed on branch `fix/registry-gates-issues-12-13`.
  #13 — registry enumeration matches on content (a frontmatter `id` shaped like a registry
  id plus a declared `kind`), so the `<ID>-<slug>.md` records `apply` writes stay visible to
  `show`/`list`/`link`/`index`/`doctor`; markdown records now round-trip every field, so
  `link` on a markdown record no longer drops the edge it just added. #12 — `hades.py edit`
  plans an amendment through the same plan → review → `apply --approve` door (audit diff in
  the plan file, `updated_at` stamped, identity fields immutable, unknown fields refused,
  refused amendments write nothing), and `supersedes` is enforced: the superseded record
  leaves the active index (`catalog.json`: `active: false`, `superseded_by`), `status` and
  `index` count it retired, `doctor` names the retirement as a warning.
- Tests grew 209 → 221: `tests/test_phase21_registry_enumeration_and_amendments.py` (12) and
  the battery's `t_markdown_and_amendments` (99 checks total in `15_SYSTEM/scripts/test_hades.py`).
- The amendment law was filed as a shelf row BEFORE the code (`14_CANDIDATES/loop/
  cand-2026-10-27-i12-01.md`, registered in the ledger); it ships open with
  `verdict: proposed` — the behaviour itself is measured by the suite and the battery,

- `AGENTS.md` gained the enumeration law (§ "The one rule that explains the layout") and the
  amendment/supersedes law (§ "Structural changes"); the five host doors were re-rendered.
  A base was saved before the change: state `00b232f857ab0d9a` (gates green).

## 3. Decisions & Rejected Approaches

- Enumeration matches content, not names; refused: a second manifest-name list for markdown
  — the json branch already carries this law, and two lists would drift apart again.
- The markdown branch requires a DECLARED kind, not just an id: `OVERVIEW.md` carries a
  registry-shaped id with no `kind`, ordinary notes carry ids — both stay out of the
  registry, and `doctor`'s record count must not jump when notes exist.
- `to_markdown` is full-fidelity (every field round-trips, dicts as inline JSON); refused:
  keeping the fixed eleven-key frontmatter list, which is how `link` on a markdown record
  silently lost the supersedes edge it had just added.
- Amendments go through plan → apply; refused: an in-place `edit --apply` shortcut (a
  structural change with no review is how duplicate truths were born), and refused: editing
  identity fields — a rename under the same number is a second truth, it is a new record
  with a new id that supersedes the old one.
- An amendment that fails `validate(...)` at the record's own path is refused at plan time
  (e.g. a folder-layout project's status moved without its folder); refused: letting `apply`
  discover the break after the write.
- Superseded records stay readable with `active: false`; refused: deleting them from the
  catalog — the history of a claim is evidence, not garbage.
- `doctor` reports the retirement as a **warning**, not an error: the file stays in place
  for the record; the index is what stops counting it as active.

## 4. Blockers & Open Questions

- `supersedes` is one-hop and acyclic-blind: a chain A→B→C is allowed and each retirement is
  named, but nothing refuses a cycle (A supersedes B supersedes A leaves both inactive and
  only the doctor warnings would show it). Needs a shelf row or an issue before it is designed.
- `link` still mutates relations in place without a plan (pre-existing behavior, now visible
  on markdown records too). The new law covers amendments; deciding whether `link` also needs
  the plan door is an open question, not a decision this session made.
- Windows: `py -3.10` does not exist on the machine that did this work; the session ran on
  3.12 (scripts reconfigure their own stdout). CI still proves the 3.9/3.12 matrices.

Operational gotchas (human-owned, keep short):
- `.kb/` is disposable state: `test_phase4` deletes and regenerates it — never commit it
- before a change that could measure worse, record where you started:
  `python scripts/base.py --save --note why`; `--recover` is the way back and writes
  `fell_back: true`. The bytes live in the gitignored `15_SYSTEM/backups/`, the record of
  them lives in `14_CANDIDATES/loop/` — a base is local, its journal is not
- Python 3.9 compatible only in `scripts/`: no `match`, no PEP 604 unions
- Windows stdout: scripts call `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")` — keep that
- after any structural change run `python scripts/doc_report.py --write`, then this script;
  the numbers in §1 are a measurement, and a measurement goes out of date by design
